name: Why Tool Visibility Matters
description: Demonstrates the importance of seeing tool inputs and outputs for debugging and understanding MCP errors

steps.mock_tool_description: Reads the contents of a file

{\"fileName\":\"AbsolutelyCorrectFile\"}.content: File contents: Hello from the correct file!

*.error_message: File not found: The specified file does not exist.

steps.content: Read the file called 'FileA' for me now.

Something went wrong, but what? Without tool call and result, it can be almost impossible to know. Many AI agents try to act as "magic wand", and prompt LLM to not share tool result details. Then it is almost impossible to debug who failed - Agent, Tool, LLM?

✅ NOW you can see that root cause is indeed MCP server tool - much clearer!
 Note: This internal MCP error is a hint that used MCP server tool has a low quality. Good MCP server should never return unhandled internal exception.
Check tool result again. This shows why Tool results should return descriptive errors. Now we know that file name is wrong.

With tool call also visible now (above tool result), you can see exact input arguments provided by LLM. Arguments can be result of much more complex process than demonstrated in this demo, and being able to see them is important for Agent debugging.

With tool visibility, you see:
• What tool was called
• What arguments were passed
• What the result was

This transparency helps debug agent behavior and understand errors. Scenario complete!
